sections.h2: Where is Hillsboro, Oregon, and how is it run?
sections.html:
Hillsboro is the county seat of Washington County, about 17 miles west of Portland and directly west of Beaverton. It sits in the Tualatin Valley, the part of the Portland metro area that locals link with the Silicon Forest.

The city was incorporated on October 19, 1876, and it switched to a council-manager system in 1923. Today a mayor and six at-large councilors set policy, and a hired city manager runs daily operations. The Census Bureau counts about 21.6 square miles of land inside city limits, so a lot of houses share a fairly compact footprint.

If you are selling here, the two offices you will deal with most are the city's planning and building staff for permits and the Washington County Assessment and Taxation office for tax bills and recording.

sections.h2: How did Hillsboro grow into the city it is now?
sections.html:
Hillsboro grew from a pioneer settlement in the 1840s into a city of more than 100,000 people, and its housing reflects each stage.

Settlers David Hill, Isaiah Kelsey and Richard Williams arrived in 1841, and the town was renamed Hillsborough in February 1850 to honor Hill. The county seat designation followed on February 5, 1850. Railroad service reached town in 1871, and an interurban electric line arrived in 1908. Ten sites in town are on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Old Scotch Church from 1876.

That is roughly 19,500 more residents in fifteen years, which explains why you see older bungalows near downtown and much newer homes on the edges of town.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers in Hillsboro?
sections.html:
Intel is the largest private employer in Hillsboro, with about 20,000 workers across its Ronler Acres, Jones Farm and Hawthorn Farm campuses. Public employers and other technology and health care firms fill out the list.

Manufacturing makes up about 24 percent of local jobs, and health care, education and social services about 15 percent. With so many jobs tied to a handful of large employers, some owners sell on a short timeline when work moves them.

sections.h2: What are the main areas of Hillsboro?
sections.html:
Hillsboro is a collection of distinct districts, and the right sale strategy for a house downtown is different from one in a newer subdivision.

  • Downtown: the original core around the county courthouse, with the oldest homes.
  • Orenco and Orenco Station: a transit-oriented neighborhood built around the light rail line.
  • Tanasbourne and Amberglen: the retail and office area on the eastern edge, near the border with Beaverton.
  • Hawthorn Farm and the Fair Complex: home to Westside Commons and the Intel campus nearby.
  • South Hillsboro: the newest planned district, annexed in recent years.
  • Witch Hazel Village, Quatama and NE 28th Avenue: comprehensive plan areas with a mix of older and newer housing.

South Hillsboro alone is master planned across about 1,400 acres, with an estimated 8,000 homes for nearly 20,000 residents, more than 285 acres of parks and open space and about 15 miles of new trails, according to the city. Sellers of older houses in neighboring areas compete with that new construction, and buyers often compare the two.

sections.h2: How do roads, light rail and the airport affect a Hillsboro house?
sections.html:
Commuters rely on Oregon Route 8 (Tualatin Valley Highway) for east-west trips, and U.S. Route 26 crosses the northeast corner of the city. Oregon Route 219, Cornelius Pass Road and Brookwood Parkway carry north-south traffic.

The MAX Blue Line has served Hillsboro since 1998 and ends at Hatfield Government Center. In 2024 the MAX Red Line was extended from the Beaverton Transit Center to the Fairgrounds station. Homes within walking distance of a station are easier to market to commuters, and homes under a busy flight path or beside a major road may need a different pitch.

Hillsboro Airport is the second-busiest airport in Oregon after Portland International, and the Oregon International Air Show is held there each summer.

sections.h2: What does Hillsboro weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Hillsboro has mild summers and a long wet season. August is the warmest month, with an average high near 81 degrees, and the coldest average high is about 46 degrees in January.

Annual precipitation is about 36 inches, spread over roughly 160 days a year, and the wettest months run from November through March. Average relative humidity is 77 percent. The all-time record high is 114 degrees, set on June 28, 2021. Summer heat spikes do happen.

Long wet seasons put the focus on a few repair items:

  • moss and worn shingles on the roof
  • gutters, downspouts and drainage near the foundation
  • damp crawl spaces and exterior wood rot
  • older windows that leak air or water

A house with these issues often needs more than a fresh coat of paint to pass a buyer's inspection, which is where as-is cash sales appeal to some owners.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when you sell a house in Hillsboro?
sections.html:
Washington County charges a real estate transfer tax of one dollar per thousand dollars of the selling price, and the county says liability is between the purchaser and the seller. The tax is due, or an exemption must be filed, within 15 days of recording, and a late penalty applies after that.

The county lists exemptions for several transaction types, including:

  • transfers by gift, devise or inheritance
  • deeds in lieu of foreclosure and court-ordered transfers
  • trustee's deeds from foreclosure
  • transfers under $13,999
  • transfers between spouses under a court order in a divorce or separation

Property tax runs on a separate schedule. Statements are mailed on or before October 25. Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15, and a full payment by November 15 earns a 3 percent discount, while a two-thirds payment earns 2 percent. When a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day counts. Value appeals go to the Board of Property Tax Appeals by December 31. Taxed value starts from the lower of real market value and maximum assessed value, and maximum assessed value can rise no more than 3 percent a year.

The county generally cannot accept prepaid property taxes, so ask your title company how the current year will be prorated at closing. Official details are on the Washington County property tax FAQ and the transfer tax exemption page.

sections.h2: What does Oregon require sellers to disclose?
sections.html:
Most Oregon sellers must hand the buyer a signed property disclosure statement, and Hillsboro sellers are no exception. Under ORS 105.464, the seller delivers the form to each buyer who makes a written offer, and the buyer then has five days after delivery to revoke the offer in writing unless that right was waived.

Some sales are excluded, including sales by court-appointed personal representatives and trustees, sales by lenders that took a property through foreclosure or a deed in lieu, and the first sale of a never-occupied home. If a seller who is not excluded refuses to provide the form, the buyer can revoke the offer at any time before closing. Disclosures reflect what the seller actually knows, so write down what you have seen, such as past leaks, repairs or permits.

sections.h2: What do Hillsboro sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers here tend to run into the same few situations, and each one changes how a sale works.

  • Rental houses: about half of Hillsboro's 42,363 housing units are renter-occupied, so many sellers are landlords with tenants in place.
  • Inherited houses: estate sales often skip the standard disclosure form and may qualify for a transfer tax exemption.
  • Deferred maintenance: wet-season damage adds up when repairs wait.
  • Timing: a job move tied to a tech employer can leave little time for a long listing.

The city's own Housing Production Strategy, readopted by council on December 2, 2025, aims to increase housing production over 2025 to 2030, so new supply is part of the picture for any seller who plans to list.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Hillsboro?
sections.html:
A cash sale means the buyer does not need a mortgage, so there is no loan approval step to wait on. You request an offer, the buyer reviews the house, and if you accept, a title company handles the paperwork and records the deed with Washington County.

The county transfer tax, the property tax proration and any liens still apply, and a title company will show them on the closing statement. Ask for the numbers in writing before you sign. If you prefer to keep the house on the market, compare a cash offer against the likely costs of repairs, agent fees and carrying the home for several months. The choice depends on your timeline and the shape of the house.

faqs.q: How many people live in Hillsboro, Oregon?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 111,126 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is up from 106,447 in the 2020 census and 91,611 in 2010.
Hillsboro is in Washington County and is its county seat. Property tax bills, recording and transfer tax all go through Washington County offices.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell a house in Hillsboro?
faqs.a: Yes. Washington County charges one dollar per thousand dollars of the selling price, and liability is between buyer and seller. The county lists exemptions, such as inheritance transfers and deeds in lieu of foreclosure.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Washington County?
faqs.a: Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15, with the next business day counting if a date lands on a weekend or holiday. Paying in full by November 15 earns a 3 percent discount.

faqs.q: Do I have to give the buyer a disclosure form in Oregon?
faqs.a: In most sales, yes. ORS 105.464 requires the seller to deliver the statement to each buyer who makes a written offer, and the buyer can revoke within five days unless that right was waived. Sales by estates, trustees and foreclosing lenders are among the exclusions.
